# Navigation of Gym menu (AH-0MV1BKZ0J00946EX)

## Problem statement

The dev-mode Gym Index (`GymIndex`) lays its launch rows out in three columns
(plain scenes | ENEMIES | Dev Utilities), but keyboard focus moves through
every row as a single linear, wrapping list. The arrow keys therefore do not
match the on-screen spatial layout: Right from the bottom of a column jumps to
the next column's first row, and there is no deliberate way to step
left/right between columns. A keyboard-only developer cannot navigate the
index the way they read it.

## Users

Developers/testers who exercise the gym scenes, and keyboard-only or
accessibility users who expect the in-canvas UI to match its visual layout.

**User stories**

- As a keyboard-only developer, I want **Left/Right** to move focus between the
  three columns, so that I can reach the column I want without tabbing through
  every row.
- As a keyboard-only developer, I want **Up/Down** to move focus within the
  current column, so that I can choose a row in that column predictably.
- As a keyboard-only developer, I want the focused row to stay highlighted and
  **Enter/Space** to launch it exactly as before, so that the new navigation
  does not break activation.
- As a maintainer, I want the grid behaviour to be **opt-in** in the shared
  focus manager, so that every other menu keeps its current linear Tab/arrow
  behaviour.

## Acceptance Criteria

- **AC1 — Opt-in grid navigation; existing behaviour unchanged.** The shared
  `FocusManager` (or a small shared helper alongside it) gains an opt-in
  column-aware navigation mode. Scenes that do not opt in keep today's linear
  Tab / Shift+Tab / arrow cycling with wrap-around. *Verification:* the
  existing `src/utils/focusManager.test.ts` passes unchanged, and a new test
  asserts the default mode is still linear.
- **AC2 — Left/Right move between Gym Index columns.** With grid navigation
  enabled, **Right** moves focus to the adjacent column on the right and
  **Left** to the adjacent column on the left, wrapping from the rightmost
  column to the leftmost and vice versa. Focus never lands on a non-row
  (title, headers or hint). *Verification:* a unit test in
  `src/scenes/GymIndex.test.ts` asserts the focused column changes on
  ArrowLeft/ArrowRight and wraps at both ends.
- **AC3 — Up/Down move within the current column.** **Down** moves focus to
  the next row in the current column and **Up** to the previous row, wrapping
  within the column (top ↔ bottom). Up/Down never change column.
  *Verification:* a unit test asserts vertical movement and per-column
  wrap-around without leaving the column.
- **AC4 — Uneven columns always land on a valid row.** The columns have
  different row counts (plain scenes: many; ENEMIES: 3; Dev Utilities: 1).
  Moving horizontally into a shorter column focuses a valid, highlighted row
  (clamping rule documented below) — never an out-of-range index or a
  non-row. *Verification:* a unit test drives focus to the bottom of the
  longest column, presses Right into the shortest column, and asserts a real
  row is focused and highlighted.
- **AC5 — Activation, pointer and ESC unchanged.** Enter/Space still activate
  the focused row through the same callback as a pointer click (plain scene,
  Fodder Enemies, Boss, Mini-Boss, Dev Utilities), pointer clicks still work
  for every row, ESC still returns to the main menu, and SHUTDOWN still
  detaches the keyboard listener and clears the focus registry.
  *Verification:* the existing GymIndex activation/pointer/ESC/shutdown tests
  remain green, plus a new test activating a row after moving between columns.
- **AC6 — Hint and documentation updated.** `GYM_INDEX_HINT` and every doc that
  enumerates keyboard navigation describe Left/Right column movement and
  Up/Down row movement. *Verification:* inspection of the hint and the updated
  docs sections.
- **AC7 — Tests, docs and full suite.** New/updated tests cover AC1–AC5. All
  related documentation is updated to reflect the changes, including code
  comments, README, and any relevant wiki or docs site entries. The full
  project test suite must pass with the new changes.

## Constraints

- Scope is the **Gym Index screen** (`GymIndex`), **not** the internal menus of
  individual gym scenes and **not** the other menu-style scenes.
- Reuse the shared `FocusManager`; do **not** add a second ad-hoc focus/key
  handler inside `GymIndex`.
- The default (non-grid) behaviour must remain the current linear behaviour
  for every other consumer (`MenuScene`, `GameOverScene`, `PauseScene`,
  `HelpScene`, `LeaderboardScene`, `TelemetryConsentScene`, and the Hangar War
  screens).
- Pointer handlers, ESC-to-menu, row ordering and the column layout (X
  positions) must not change.
- No CI/CD pipeline tests (per intake convention). `CHANGELOG.md` is excluded
  (managed by the ship skill).
- No new npm dependencies.

## Existing state

- `src/scenes/GymIndex.ts` renders three columns and registers every row with
  the shared `FocusManager` in reading order (plain scenes → ENEMIES → Dev
  Utilities). `GYM_INDEX_HINT` currently reads
  `tab/arrows move · enter/space select · ESC returns to menu`.
- `src/utils/focusManager.ts` maps Tab / Shift+Tab and **every** arrow key
  onto linear `cycleFocus(±1)` with wrap-around; it has no notion of columns or
  axis. It is used by `MenuScene`, `GameOverScene`, `PauseScene`, `HelpScene`,
  `LeaderboardScene`, `TelemetryConsentScene` and the Hangar War screens.
- `GymIndex` exposes test accessors `listedScenes`, `listedEnemyScenes`,
  `listedDevUtilityScenes`, `getFocusedIndex`, `getFocusedLabel` and
  `getFocusControlCount`. Column X positions are exported as
  `GYM_INDEX_COLUMN_X`.
- `src/scenes/GymIndex.test.ts` already has a keyboard-navigation block that
  asserts the current linear order and wrap; those arrow assertions will need
  updating to the new semantics (Tab/activation/ESC coverage is kept).
- 2-D/grid navigation was explicitly deferred in AH-0MUDZFBYY008P7ZE (linear
  cycling shipped instead); this item is the follow-up that delivers it.

## Desired change

1. Extend the shared `FocusManager` with an **opt-in** column-aware mode (for
   example `attachKeyboard(scene, { navigation: 'grid', columns: [...] })` or an
   `attachGridKeyboard(scene, columns)` helper). Columns are ordered lists of
   controls (or focus indices) in visual order; the default path stays exactly
   as today.
2. In `GymIndex.create()`, register the existing three columns with grid mode,
   using the same `registerRow` activation callbacks.
3. Implement the horizontal/vertical movement rules (including wrap and
   shorter-column clamping) and keep Enter/Space activation unchanged.
4. Update `GYM_INDEX_HINT`, the module doc comment and the README
   keyboard-navigation / Gym Index sections.
5. Update/extend `src/utils/focusManager.test.ts` and
   `src/scenes/GymIndex.test.ts` to cover grid mode while keeping linear mode
   covered.

## Key Files (predicted)

- `src/utils/focusManager.ts` — add opt-in grid/column navigation while
  preserving the current linear default.
- `src/scenes/GymIndex.ts` — opt into grid navigation, pass the three columns,
  update the hint and module doc comment.
- `src/utils/focusManager.test.ts` — cover grid-mode movement and confirm the
  linear default is untouched.
- `src/scenes/GymIndex.test.ts` — cover Left/Right column movement (with wrap),
  Up/Down within-column movement, uneven-column clamping, activation after a
  column move, and the updated hint.
- `README.md` — update the keyboard-only navigation section and the Gym Index
  section (~lines 391 and ~417) to describe column/row arrows.
- `docs/ENEMY_DESIGN_AND_IMPLEMENTATION.md` — §8.5 keyboard-operability note if
  it enumerates Gym Index navigation.

## Related work

- AH-0MUDZFBYY008P7ZE — Gym scenes index not navigable by keyboard (delivered
  linear `FocusManager` navigation; explicitly deferred 2-D/grid navigation).
  *Completed.*
- AH-0MUBZT64O0056BRY — Reusable in-canvas focus manager (the shared utility
  to extend). *Completed.*
- AH-0MV13G5EV008D41E — Single enemy gym scene with in-panel selector;
  established the current three-column index layout. *Completed.*
- AH-0MUGXDVPH005TIZL — Dev Utilities gym scene / column. *Completed.*
- AH-0MU9LKQEP008LCX9 — Keyboard only control (umbrella). *Completed.*

## Risks & assumptions

**Risks**

- **FocusManager regression.** The utility is used by eight scenes; a careless
  change could alter their arrow-key behaviour. Mitigation: opt-in mode only,
  default unchanged, plus the existing FocusManager tests and the full-suite
  gate.
- **Test churn.** The existing GymIndex keyboard tests assert linear arrow
  order; they must be updated to the new arrow semantics while keeping
  Tab/activation/ESC coverage. Mitigation: keep Tab's behaviour explicit and
  test both models.
- **Uneven-column UX.** A naive clamp can make focus jump unexpectedly when
  moving to a shorter column and back. Mitigation: document the rule and test
  it; sticky per-column row memory is a small, contained follow-up if wanted.
- **Scope creep.** Grid navigation for other scenes (Leaderboard grid, hex
  map) or mouse-free gym internals is out of scope; record as linked
  follow-ups rather than expanding this change.

**Assumptions (confirmed by producer, 2026-11-07)**

- Grid mode is **opt-in** and **GymIndex-only** in this change.
- Left/Right **wrap** between columns (rightmost → leftmost and vice versa),
  matching the existing wrap convention.
- Up/Down **wrap within the current column** (top → bottom and bottom → top)
  and never change column.
- On entering a shorter column, focus **clamps to the last valid row** of that
  column (no per-column row memory in this change).
- **Tab keeps its current linear cycling** through all rows in reading order;
  only the arrow keys become grid-aware.
- Activation (Enter/Space), pointer handling and ESC behaviour are unchanged.

## Appendix: Clarifying questions & answers

The producer answered all five questions with option **(a)** — the recommended
option — confirming the working assumptions recorded during the auto-dispatched
intake.

**Q1 — Should Left/Right wrap between columns, or clamp at the outer
columns?**

- Answer (producer): **(a) Wrap** — rightmost column → leftmost, and vice
  versa. Confirms the working assumption. Source: interactive reply,
  2026-11-07.

**Q2 — Should Up/Down stay within the current column, or move across columns
at the top/bottom edge?**

- Answer (producer): **(a) Stay within the column and wrap top ↔ bottom.**
  Confirms the working assumption. Source: interactive reply, 2026-11-07.

**Q3 — How should focus behave when moving into a shorter column (for example
Dev Utilities has a single row)?**

- Answer (producer): **(a) Clamp to the last valid row of the target column;
  no per-column "remembered row".** Confirms the working assumption. Source:
  interactive reply, 2026-11-07.

**Q4 — Should Tab remain linear cycling through all rows, or also become
grid-aware?**

- Answer (producer): **(a) Keep Tab linear; only the arrow keys are
  grid-aware.** Confirms the working assumption. Source: interactive reply,
  2026-11-07.

**Q5 — Should grid navigation be a shared opt-in `FocusManager` mode, or local
to `GymIndex`?**

- Answer (producer): **(a) Shared opt-in `FocusManager` mode, with the default
  linear behaviour unchanged.** Confirms the working assumption. Source:
  interactive reply, 2026-11-07. Research: inspected
  `src/utils/focusManager.ts` (linear-only today) and its consumers; no
  existing grid mode.

## Related work (automated report)

### Related work items
- **AH-0MUDZFBYY008P7ZE** – Gym scenes index not navigable by keyboard (completed)
- **AH-0MV13G5EV008D41E** – Single enemy gym scene with in-panel enemy selector dropdown (completed)
- **AH-0MUE24XVY009HWRH** – Tests: CSV codec (parse, serialise, coerce, validate) (completed)

### Repository file matches
- `docs/Game Design Document.md` — matched: ac1, ac2, ac3, ac4, ac5 (+353 more)
- `README.md` — matched: 0mudzfbyy008p7ze, 0mv13g5ev008d41e, ac1, ac2, ac3 (+337 more)

# Objective

Give asteroid entities the **lowest render depth** ("furthest away" z value) of
any foreground gameplay object, so a drifting rock always draws behind the
player ship, every other enemy, bullets, minerals and power-ups — while still
drawing above the background and juice layers. One named constant, applied once
on the shared `Asteroid` entity, so the game and every asteroid-bearing gym stay
in parity by construction.

## Problem statement

Asteroids are inert, drifting **world hazards** that should read as distant
scenery, but they currently render at the default gameplay depth (`0`) — the
same depth as the player, every enemy, minerals and power-ups — so their visual
order is decided purely by scene display-list insertion order. Because the
scheduled spawner releases asteroids *during* a wave (after the formation
enemies are added) their containers are appended last and therefore draw **on
top of** ships and other enemies. A large rock can visibly occlude a scout or
the player, which reads as the rock being in front of the action rather than
behind it.

## Users / user stories

- **As a player**, when an asteroid drifts across a formation of enemies, I want
  it to pass *behind* them so the action stays legible and the rock reads as
  distant scenery, not a foreground object.
- **As a player**, I want bullets, minerals and power-ups to stay clearly
  visible above asteroids so pickups and shots are never hidden by a rock.
- **As a developer / gym author**, I want the asteroid depth defined once on the
  shared entity so the game and every gym render it identically with no
  per-scene wiring.

## Acceptance Criteria

- Asteroid entities render at the **lowest foreground depth**: strictly below
  every other gameplay object (player, all other enemy archetypes, bullets,
  minerals, power-ups) and strictly above every background layer
  (`BACKGROUND_DEPTH`, `BACKGROUND_DIM_DEPTH`, `BACKGROUND_WARP_DEPTH`).
- The depth is a **single named constant** (e.g. `ASTEROID_DEPTH`) exported
  from `src/core/constants.ts` and applied **once** in the `Asteroid`
  constructor, so all spawn paths — the scheduled spawner
  (`createAsteroidFromEvent`), `PlayScene.spawnAsteroidAt`, the shared
  `splitAsteroid` children, and every gym spawn — inherit the same value with no
  per-call wiring.
- A focused unit test asserts that a newly constructed `Asteroid` **and** a
  split child both expose `depth === ASTEROID_DEPTH`, that the value is
  strictly less than the gameplay baseline (`0`) and strictly greater than the
  background layers, and that the existing **intra-entity** layer order
  (body/force-field/explosion) is unchanged.
- Gym↔game parity: an asteroid spawned through the shared seam in the game and
  in an asteroid-bearing gym resolve the identical depth (pinned by a test and
  the parity docs), so no scene can diverge.
- All related documentation is updated to reflect the change — code comments,
  `docs/ENEMY_DESIGN_AND_IMPLEMENTATION.md` (E6 asteroid section and/or render
  layering note), `docs/GYM_PARITY.md` where relevant, and the GDD if it
  documents render layering — and the full project test suite passes.

## Constraints

- The change must live on the **shared `Asteroid` entity** (and a shared
  constant), never on a per-scene spawn path, to satisfy the gym↔game parity
  convention in `AGENTS.md` § Game Architecture Conventions.
- The asteroid must stay **above** the background photo, its dim overlay and the
  hyperspace-warp layers; "lowest" means lowest **foreground** layer, not below
  the backdrop.
- Do **not** change the asteroid's intra-container child depths (body `1`,
  force-field `1.5`, explosion `2`) or their relative order — only the
  container's own scene depth.
- No gameplay behaviour change: motion, wrapping, splitting, collision, scoring
  and audio are untouched. This is a **render-order-only** change.
- Must not affect non-asteroid enemies, the boss, bullets or pickups.

## Existing state

- **Phaser render ordering.** In Phaser (v4.2.1) a `GameObject`'s `depth`
  property is the "z-index" used for display-list render order; higher depth
  renders on top. `setDepth()` is the mechanism.
- **Depth layers already defined** in `src/core/constants.ts`:
  `BACKGROUND_DEPTH = -1000`, `BACKGROUND_DIM_DEPTH = -950`,
  `BACKGROUND_WARP_DEPTH = -900`, `HUD_DEPTH = 1000`; and in
  `src/core/constants.ts` / entity modules: `MINERAL_DEPTH = 2`,
  `MYSTERY_UFO_DRONE_DEPTH = 2`, bullets at `3`.
- **Every enemy (including `Asteroid`) extends `BaseEnemy`, a
  `Phaser.GameObjects.Container`,** and none of them set the container's own
  depth, so they all render at the default gameplay depth `0`. Their internal
  child graphics set depths **within** the container (`src/entities/BaseEnemy.ts`:
  body `1`, force-field `1.5`, explosion `2`).
- **All asteroid spawn paths construct the `Asteroid` entity directly**:
  `src/scenes/core/asteroidHazard.ts::createAsteroidFromEvent`,
  `PlayScene.spawnAsteroidAt`, and `src/scenes/core/asteroidSplit.ts`
  (`splitAsteroid` children). Gym spawns go through the same entity/factory. A
  depth set in the entity constructor therefore covers every path.
- There is **no existing z/depth column** in `src/data/enemy-configs.csv` and no
  documented asteroid render-order convention in the design docs — this item
  establishes that convention.

## Desired change

1. Add a named `ASTEROID_DEPTH` constant in `src/core/constants.ts` (value `-1`
   unless the implementer has a reason to pick another value in the open interval
   `(BACKGROUND_WARP_DEPTH, 0)`), documented as "lowest foreground gameplay
   layer: below every ship/enemy/bullet/pickup, above the background".
2. In the `Asteroid` constructor, call `this.setDepth(ASTEROID_DEPTH)` once
   (after `super(...)` / `addSharedGraphics()`), so the container renders below
   every default-depth (`0`) gameplay object.
3. Add a focused unit test (in `src/entities/Asteroid.test.ts` or a dedicated
   depth test) that pins the depth on a fresh asteroid and on a split child, and
   asserts the ordering against the gameplay baseline and background constants.
4. Add/extend a gym-parity assertion so the depth cannot drift between the game
   and an asteroid-bearing gym; record the layer in the parity docs.
5. Update the relevant docs/comments to describe the new lowest-foreground
   layer.

## Key Files (predicted)

- `src/core/constants.ts` — Add the exported `ASTEROID_DEPTH` constant alongside
  the existing depth constants (with a doc comment describing the layer).
- `src/entities/Asteroid.ts` — Apply `this.setDepth(ASTEROID_DEPTH)` once in the
  constructor; note the layer in the module/class doc comment.
- `src/entities/Asteroid.test.ts` — New assertions: fresh asteroid depth, split
  child depth, strict ordering vs gameplay baseline (`0`) and background
  layers, intra-entity layer order unchanged.
- `src/scenes/core/asteroidHazard.ts` — Verify the shared spawn seam carries the
  depth (likely no change; the entity constructor owns it) and cover it in the
  test.
- `docs/ENEMY_DESIGN_AND_IMPLEMENTATION.md` — E6 asteroid section: record that
  asteroids render at the lowest foreground depth (layer note).
- `docs/GYM_PARITY.md` — Record the shared render-depth invariant where gym↔game
  parity is described (if a per-gym row is the right home).

## Related work

- **AH-0MU8BZ2ZM004J47F** — Asteroids as an enemy (origin of the `Asteroid`
  entity, tiers, splitting, no-fire guarantee).
- **AH-0MW5088LA007XYQM** — Shared asteroid silhouette palette and single atlas
  (asteroid *rendering* work; the atlas/batching layer that this depth change
  must not disturb).
- **AH-0MW508UAQ002IC5N** — Asteroid rendering parity guard and docs row
  (precedent for an asteroid render-parity guard + docs update).
- **AH-0MVSEB7SA004B26C** — Shared background layer in combat core (the
  background depth layers the asteroid must stay above).
- **AH-0MUCST3BS0007CPT** — Mineral collectable entity and constants (precedent
  for an entity-owned depth constant, `MINERAL_DEPTH = 2`).

## Related work (automated report)

### Related work items
- **AH-0MV8BR9Y70079TKC** – Wormhole appears away from player (completed)
- **AH-0MT9FRVF00086TO3** – Ship configuration file: load and save values (completed)
- **AH-0MUCG5T7S001F9MQ** – Keep asteroids moving and collidable during the transition (Phase 2) (completed)

### Repository file matches
- `README.md` — matched: asteroids, away, lowest, make, value
- `docs/ENEMY_DESIGN_AND_IMPLEMENTATION.md` — matched: asteroids, away, furthest, make, value
- `docs/Game Design Document.md` — matched: asteroids, away, lowest, make, value

## Risks & assumptions

- **Assumption (layer scope).** "Lowest (furthest away) z value" means the
  lowest **foreground** layer: below the player, other enemies, bullets,
  minerals and power-ups, but above the background/dim/warp layers. Rendering
  below the backdrop would make asteroids invisible, which is not the intent.
- **Assumption (value).** `-1` is used as the depth because it is the only
  simple integer strictly between the background warp layer (`-900`) and the
  gameplay baseline (`0`); if another foreground layer is later introduced
  between them, this constant is the single place to re-tune.
- **Risk (occlusion of collision feedback).** Placing rocks behind ships means
  an impact/explosion at the exact overlap point can be briefly occluded by the
  ship in front. Explosion particles/impacts are drawn at higher depths
  (`explosionGraphics` depth `2` within the container, plus shared impact VFX at
  positive depths), so feedback still lands above the ship in practice; verify
  during implementation.
- **Risk (parity drift).** If the depth were applied per-scene instead of on the
  shared entity, the game and a gym could diverge. Mitigation: apply it once on
  the entity and pin it with a parity test.
- **Scope-creep risk.** A full y-sorted pseudo-3D layering system for all
  gameplay entities is **out of scope**; this item only gives asteroids a fixed
  lowest foreground layer. Any broader depth-sorting work should be raised as a
  separate work item rather than folded in here.

## Appendix: Clarifying questions & answers

- **Q: What does "lowest (furthest away) z value" mean in this codebase
  — which layer should asteroids sit below?**
  — **Answer (assumption, recorded for producer confirmation):** The lowest
  **foreground** gameplay layer — below the player, all other enemies, bullets,
  minerals and power-ups, but above the background photo/dim/warp layers. The
  parenthetical "(furthest away)" is read as "most distant foreground object",
  not "behind the backdrop". Research: Phaser `depth` is the z-index
  (`node_modules/phaser/types/phaser.d.ts`); `src/core/constants.ts` defines
  background depths `-1000/-950/-900`, gameplay baseline `0`, minerals/bullets
  at positive depths, HUD `1000`; no existing asteroid render-order convention
  is documented in the GDD or `docs/ENEMY_DESIGN_AND_IMPLEMENTATION.md`.
  Source: repo inspection during intake.
- **Q: Should asteroids also render behind other enemies only, but above the
  player?**
  — **Answer (assumption):** No. "Lowest" is taken literally — asteroids are the
  most distant foreground object, so they render behind the player too. Source:
  intake reasoning; flagged here so the producer can correct it.

## Problem

`node_modules/.vite` accumulates orphaned `deps_temp_<hash>` directories whenever a Vite dep optimisation is interrupted or collides — at intake there were 98 (141 MB), now **95 dirs / 158 MB total in `node_modules/.vite`**. They are pure cache debris: each is a partially written pre-bundle. The epic's AC3 timing work is unaffected functionally, but the debris wastes disk, slows directory scans, and is evidence that dep optimisation is re-running/colliding (which is one source of the transform/import variance measured in AH-0MVF6Y29M005TEOG).

## Why this was not fixed inline

`node_modules` is **shared by every worktree on this host via symlink**; deleting the cache while another agent's suite is mid-run can corrupt that run. The producer rule 'never destroy another agent's work' applies, so the cleanup needs a safe, quiescent mechanism rather than an opportunistic `rm -rf`.

## Expected change

A small, documented, safe cleanup path — e.g. `scripts/clean-vite-cache.mjs` that:
- refuses to run when any `vitest`/`vite` process is alive (or requires `--force`),
- removes only `deps_temp_*` (never the valid `deps/` bundle or `deps_ssr`),
- reports bytes reclaimed, and
- is documented in `docs/dev/test-suite-timing.md` (cache-hygiene section) and optionally wired into `scripts/hygiene_check.sh`.

## Acceptance Criteria

- **AC1:** A read-only `--dry-run` (default) reports the orphaned `deps_temp_*` count and bytes; `--apply` removes only those dirs and prints the reclaimed bytes.
- **AC2:** The script refuses to delete while a `vitest`/`vite` process is running unless `--force` is passed, and is covered by tests (dry-run classification, refusal path) that do not require a real cache.
- **AC3:** Documentation states why the cache is shared across worktrees and why the quiescence guard exists.
- **AC4:** After `--apply` on an idle host, `npx vitest run --project unit` still passes (cache regenerates cleanly).

## References

- AH-0MVF6Y29M005TEOG — measured the transform/import cost and rejected the optimizer/isolate/pool variants; notes the collision evidence.
- `scripts/hygiene_check.sh` — the existing periodic hygiene report this could extend.

## Goal

Crash resilience for dev telemetry: stream each flushed telemetry batch to the
dev server **during the run** so that a page reload/crash mid-run loses at most
one in-flight batch instead of the whole run's un-uploaded tail.

Today the dev JSONL sink is an in-memory, per-run buffer
(`createMemoryLineWriter()`, AH-0MVIRYGD1000JVY3) that is POSTed **once at run
end** (`uploadDevTelemetry`). A crash or reload before that POST loses the
entire run; streaming bounds the loss to the batch in flight (~64 records,
~1.3 s of play at default settings) and removes the page-reload regression that
the old localStorage-backed sink accidentally masked.

This item is the explicitly deferred follow-up to the in-memory-sink work
(`discovered-from:AH-0MVIRYGD1000JVY3`); it was parked until that item landed
(it shipped in v0.1.15) and must not be implemented concurrently with it in the
same worktree.

## Problem statement

The dev telemetry pipeline buffers records in memory, flushes them in batches of
`DEFAULT_TELEMETRY_BATCH_SIZE` (64) into the per-run in-memory sink, and only
uploads the whole buffer at run end from `PlayScene._finishRun()` →
`flushAndUploadDevTelemetry()`. Browser memory is volatile: a page reload or
renderer crash between the last flush and the run-end POST discards the entire
run. The old localStorage sink survived a reload (until the quota filled), so
moving to memory introduced a detectable regression for interrupted runs.

The production sink is **not** affected: `HttpTelemetryTransport` already
streams each recorded batch to the configured remote endpoint with retry and
backoff. Only the dev (`jsonl`) path uploads at run end.

## Users

- **Developer / operator running a dev session** — "As a developer playing or
  recording a dev run, when the page reloads or crashes mid-run, I want the dev
  server to already have all but the last second or so of telemetry, so a long
  session is not lost and I do not have to reproduce it."
- **Developer running the dev CLI tooling** — "As a developer, I want
  `npm run record`, `npm run capture` and `npm run verify-dev-telemetry` to
  keep working exactly as they do, reading the full run from the page buffer at
  run end, so streaming does not break my existing workflow."
- **Maintainer of the dev telemetry server** — "As a maintainer, I want the dev
  server to store each run's records exactly once in one session file and to
  run the automatic evaluation once per run, so partial and final uploads
  cannot double-count or trigger duplicate evaluations."

## Existing state (verified in code)

- `src/telemetry/sinks.ts` — `createMemoryLineWriter()` is the `jsonl` sink's
  default line writer: an unbounded in-memory `string[]` with `read()`/`reset()`.
  `JsonlTelemetrySink.write()` serialises a batch to lines and appends them;
  `read()` returns the whole buffer as NDJSON, `reset()` clears it.
- `src/telemetry/recorder.ts` — `BufferedTelemetryRecorder` drains a 512-record
  ring buffer into batches of `batchSize` (64) and hands them to the sink on a
  serialised `writeChain`. `startRun()` clears the ring buffer and resets the
  sink, so a run's recording is run-scoped.
- `src/telemetry/devUpload.ts` — `uploadDevTelemetry()` reads the whole buffer
  through the injected `readSink` seam and POSTs it once at run end to
  `POST /api/telemetry/upload` (NDJSON, same-origin), fire-and-forget, with an
  8 MiB CDP-message cap (`DEFAULT_MAX_DEV_UPLOAD_MESSAGE_BYTES`, ceiling 16 MiB;
  over-cap bodies are skipped with one actionable line). The buffer is left
  intact after a successful upload.
- `src/scenes/PlayScene.ts` — `_initTelemetry()` installs the dev-gated
  `window.__aiHellTelemetry = { read() }` accessor (returning the whole run
  buffer) and calls `startRun`; `_finishRun()` calls
  `flushAndUploadDevTelemetry()`, which flushes the recorder and then uploads the
  whole buffer.
- `vite/plugins/telemetryUploadPlugin.ts` — the `POST /api/telemetry/upload`
  middleware validates the body with `parseRecording()`, stores it as one
  `recordings/session-<stamp>.jsonl` (collision-safe), and enqueues **one**
  background evaluation per upload. `apply: 'serve'` only; the endpoint is
  absent from a production bundle (bundle-hygiene marker).
- Dev CLI tooling — `scripts/record-session.mjs` and
  `scripts/capture-gameplay.mjs` read the run at run end through
  `window.__aiHellTelemetry` (chunked, bounded reads);
  `scripts/verify-dev-telemetry.mjs` plays a run, then asserts a new
  `recordings/session-*.jsonl`, ≥1 `POST /api/telemetry/upload` all 200, one
  `eval-output/uploaded/<stamp>/` with `human-balance-report.json`, a non-empty
  page buffer, and zero uploads/recordings when the share setting is off.
- Pinned contract — `src/telemetry/devUpload.test.ts` pins "buffer content left
  intact after a successful upload"; `verify-dev-telemetry.mjs` pins
  `session-*.jsonl` naming and one evaluation per run.

## Desired change

**Recommended design: a per-batch part protocol on the existing endpoint**
(option 1 of the item's proposed design), rather than a heartbeat/checkpoint
(option 2). Option 1 streams every flushed batch, so the ≤1-batch bound holds
without a separate recovery-on-demand flow; a heartbeat still needs a reload
recovery path and cannot beat option 1's bound unless it, too, fires per batch.

### Client (game)

1. **Observe every flushed batch.** Add a dev-only post-flush observer to the
   dev JSONL sink (e.g. an optional `onFlush(deltaNdjson)` callback in
   `TelemetrySinkDeps`/`JsonlTelemetrySink`) invoked after a batch is appended,
   carrying only that batch's NDJSON lines. The sink buffer is **never cleared
   mid-run** — only an upload watermark advances.
2. **Stream parts in order.** A dev-only streamer (`src/telemetry/devStream.ts`,
   loaded through the `devMode` gate like `loadDevTelemetryUploader`) POSTs each
   delta one at a time (serialised chain), with `runKey` (generated at
   `startRun` from `startedAt`+`runSeed`, e.g. `<startedAt>-<runSeed>`),
   `offset` (cumulative record count already confirmed by the server) and a
   `final` flag on the last part.
3. **Exactly-once by server-authoritative offset.** The streamer advances its
   watermark only when the server confirms the new cumulative appended count.
   A part whose 2xx was lost is re-sent from the last confirmed offset and the
   server drops the already-appended prefix; a gap (`offset` beyond the
   server's count) is rejected so the client re-syncs. Parts are serialised so
   records never interleave out of order.
4. **Offline/unreachable.** A failed part does not advance the watermark; the
   unconfirmed delta stays in the (never-cleared) in-memory buffer and is
   retried — with light bounded backoff to avoid hammering a down server. At
   run end the final part carries whatever remains beyond the confirmed offset,
   so an outage degrades to today's single run-end upload (still subject to the
   8 MiB CDP cap).
5. **Run end.** `flushAndUploadDevTelemetry()` flushes the recorder, sends the
   final part (`final: true`) and the server finalises the run's session file and
   enqueues exactly one evaluation. `window.__aiHellTelemetry.read()` continues
   to return the full run after run end (unchanged CLI behaviour).

### Server (dev only)

1. **Part protocol on the same path.** Discriminate parts with an explicit
   marker (header or query flag) on `POST /api/telemetry/upload` so
   `verify-dev-telemetry.mjs` (which matches that path) observes them and the
   bundle-hygiene marker stays valid. Without the marker, the existing
   whole-file behaviour is unchanged (store `session-<stamp>.jsonl`, evaluate
   once) — preserving the current contract and the production-preview test.
2. **Stage parts off the `session-*.jsonl` glob.** Append part records to
   `recordings/parts/<runKey>.jsonl` (outside the `session-*.jsonl` pattern, so a
   mid-run session is never mistaken for a completed recording by
   `verify-dev-telemetry` or `recordings()` helpers). Append only records beyond
   the stored count (dedupe by offset); reject a gap with the current count.
3. **Finalise once.** On `final: true`, rename the staged file to the existing
   collision-safe `recordings/session-<stamp>.jsonl` name and enqueue **one**
   evaluation (existing `EvaluationQueue`). Return 200 JSON with the merged
   record count.
4. **Crashed runs.** A run that never sends a final part leaves only
   `recordings/parts/<runKey>.jsonl` — valid NDJSON, readable by
   `scripts/inspect-telemetry.mjs` and evaluable with `evaluate.mjs --human`, but
   not auto-evaluated (evaluation belongs to complete runs). Partial cleanup is
   recorded as discovered work, not scope.

## Acceptance Criteria

1. **Loss bound (AC1).** A page reload/crash mid-run, followed by the run's
   final upload, loses no more than the records not yet confirmed by the dev
   server — the in-flight batch (≤64 records / ~1.3 s at defaults) plus the ring
   buffer's unflushed tail (<64 records); everything confirmed is recoverable
   from the dev server. The bound holds while the dev server is reachable; during
   an outage the un-uploaded tail remains in memory and is retried at run end.
2. **Exactly once + one evaluation (AC2).** A run's stored session file contains
   each record exactly once across any mix of partial and final uploads (no
   duplication, no gaps from lost/retried 2xx responses) and the automatic
   evaluation runs exactly once per completed run.
3. **CLI tooling unchanged (AC3).** `npm run record`, `npm run capture` and
   `npm run verify-dev-telemetry` behave unchanged — the page buffer is never
   cleared mid-run and `window.__aiHellTelemetry.read()` returns the full run
   after run end; `verify-dev-telemetry.mjs` passes unchanged (one
   `session-*.jsonl` per run, one evaluation artifact set, all dev uploads 200,
   zero uploads/recordings when the share setting is off). `scripts/inspect-telemetry.mjs`
   behaviour is unchanged.
4. **Testing/validation.** New hermetic tests cover: the streamer sends one part
   per flush in order; a lost 2xx is retried from the last confirmed offset and
   the server deduplicates (no duplication, no gaps); an unreachable server
   leaves the watermark unadvanced and the buffer intact; run end finalises once
   and triggers one evaluation; the sink buffer is never cleared mid-run; and
   `startRun` starts a fresh run key (no cross-run mixing). Server-side tests
   cover part staging, gap rejection, finalise/rename and single-evaluation.
5. **Docs.** `docs/TELEMETRY.md`, `docs/dev/gameplay-capture.md` and
   `docs/dev/recording-and-replay.md` describe the streaming part protocol, the
   loss bound, the offline/retry behaviour and the crashed-run partial
   location/semantics. All related documentation is updated to reflect the
   changes, including code comments, README, and any relevant wiki or docs site
   entries.
6. **Dev-only containment.** Streaming is behind the existing dev gate and is
   absent from a production bundle (bundle-hygiene markers updated for any new
   protocol strings); the opt-out setting produces zero part uploads.
7. **Full suite.** Full project test suite must pass with the new changes (via
   the test-skill runner; enforced at the dev-push gate).

## Constraints

- **Dev-only.** Reuse `isDevTelemetryUploadEnabled` / `loadDevTelemetryUploader`;
  no production bundle may contain the part protocol or the streamer.
- **Preserve the page buffer.** Never clear the in-memory sink mid-run — the CLI
  tooling and `verify-dev-telemetry`'s non-empty-buffer assertion depend on it;
  only the upload watermark moves.
- **Same endpoint path** (`/api/telemetry/upload`) plus an explicit part marker,
  so `verify-dev-telemetry.mjs` observes the parts and the existing
  bundle-hygiene marker remains valid. Keep the whole-file (no-marker) contract
  byte-compatible.
- **Bounded bodies.** Each part is ≤1 batch (tens of KB). The run-end tail after
  an offline stretch still respects the 8 MiB CDP-message cap (client) and the
  16 MiB server body bound; over-cap behaviour keeps today's actionable skip.
- **Ordered, exactly-once parts.** Serialise part POSTs; dedupe by a
  server-authoritative cumulative offset; reject gaps.
- **No cross-run mixing.** A new `runKey` and a buffer reset at `startRun`; a
  crashed run's partial is never merged into another run.
- **No new runtime dependency.** Node built-ins and already-imported modules
  only; tests write only into `mkdtempSync` temp dirs (suite-write guard).
- **Repository boundaries.** Do not edit `.pi/`, `skill/`, `command/` or other
  agent infrastructure.
- **Coordination.** Do not implement concurrently in the same worktree as the
  in-memory-sink item (already shipped) or the CLI-local salvage item
  (`AH-0MVVH57LL00038WQ`).

## Key Files (predicted)

- `src/telemetry/sinks.ts` — add the optional post-flush observer seam on the
  dev JSONL sink (delta NDJSON per batch); keep the buffer/`reset()` semantics.
- `src/telemetry/devStream.ts` *(new)* — dev-only streaming uploader: serialised
  part POSTs, watermark/offset tracking, bounded retry/backoff, final part.
- `src/telemetry/devUpload.ts` — evolve the run-end uploader into the final-part
  sender (or add a `final` mode), keeping the 8 MiB cap and fire-and-forget
  contract.
- `src/telemetry/devMode.ts` — dev-gated loader for the streamer (static
  elimination in production, mirroring `loadDevTelemetryUploader`).
- `src/scenes/PlayScene.ts`, `src/scenes/core/runTelemetry.ts` — wire the
  streamer to the sink observer and the run-end final part; keep
  `window.__aiHellTelemetry` returning the full buffer.
- `src/telemetry/recorder.ts` — expose a flush/batch observer only if the sink
  seam alone is insufficient.
- `vite/plugins/telemetryUploadPlugin.ts` — part protocol: run-keyed staging,
  offset dedupe, finalise/rename, single evaluation; whole-file path unchanged.
- Tests — `src/telemetry/devStream.test.ts` *(new)*, `sinks.test.ts`,
  `devUpload.test.ts`, `recorder.test.ts`, `vite/plugins/telemetryUploadPlugin.test.ts`,
  `src/scenes/PlaySceneTelemetry.test.ts`; `scripts/verify-dev-telemetry.mjs`
  stays green unchanged.
- `scripts/check-bundle-hygiene.mjs` — add/confirm forbidden markers for any new
  dev protocol string.
- Docs — `docs/TELEMETRY.md`, `docs/dev/gameplay-capture.md`,
  `docs/dev/recording-and-replay.md`.

## Related work

- **Control scheme reverts to Asteroids after re-opening Settings** (AH-0MVIRYGD1000JVY3, completed) — the in-memory, per-run dev sink this item extends; it explicitly deferred incremental upload here.
- **Recorder silently loses a session when the browser is closed instead of Ctrl+C** (AH-0MVVH57LL00038WQ, plan_complete) — **partial overlap, different scope**: CLI-local checkpoint/salvage of a mid-run close. Its decision D1 records that if page streaming ships first, its checkpoint becomes redundant and its salvage message should point at the server-side partial. This item changes what the **server** has; that item changes what the **CLI** does when the page dies. Its AC requires `record-session` behaviour unchanged, which this item preserves.
- **Game-side uploader fired at run end** (AH-0MVBMRK6X0069QDI, completed) — the `uploadDevTelemetry` flow being extended; its 8 MiB CDP cap still applies.
- **Dev-only telemetry gate helper + enforcement scan** (AH-0MVBMR0BG0005BBI, completed) and **Dev collection-on-by-default in stock dev mode** (AH-0MVBMRIB800201KK, completed) — the gate the streamer must reuse and the opt-out path it must honour.
- **Dev recording, analysis and replay/ghost tooling** (AH-0MUY08W7Y004GATZ, completed) — the CLI tools whose buffer-read contract AC3 preserves.
- **Capture crashes on long full-run clips: Playwright CDP pipe overflows** (AH-0MVN06MS9007LRKE, completed) and **Cap the dev upload message size** (AH-0MVNVGP55002G0KH, completed) — why every upload stays bounded.
- **Production telemetry: opt-in consent, privacy, remote sink** (AH-0MUY08Y9P005ER7A, completed) — `HttpTelemetryTransport` already streams batches with retry/backoff; the dev path should mirror its semantics.

## Risks & assumptions

- **Risk — harness coupling.** Any part stored under the `session-*.jsonl` glob
  mid-run breaks `verify-dev-telemetry.mjs` (it takes the newest match as the
  finished recording). Mitigation: stage under `recordings/parts/` and rename on
  finalise.
- **Risk — exactly-once subtlety.** A lost 2xx means the client cannot know
  whether the part landed. Mitigation: server-authoritative cumulative offset,
  client advances only on confirmation, re-send from the confirmed offset,
  server truncates the already-appended prefix and rejects gaps.
- **Risk — ordering.** Concurrent parts could interleave records. Mitigation:
  serialise the part chain (as the recorder already serialises sink writes).
- **Risk — offline backlog.** A long outage grows the run-end tail until it hits
  the 8 MiB CDP cap and is skipped (today's behaviour). Accepted for dev
  telemetry; documented.
- **Risk — bundle hygiene.** A new protocol string could leak into `dist/`.
  Mitigation: extend `scripts/check-bundle-hygiene.mjs` forbidden markers and
  keep the streamer behind the statically-eliminated dev loader.
- **Risk — scope creep.** Partial janitors, a server-side recovery UI, IndexedDB,
  alerting, or changing flush cadence are out of scope — record them as
  `discovered-from:AH-0MVJUAADW0033QBD` items instead.
- **Assumption A1.** Defaults: full sampling, ~50.8 ticks/s, 64-record batches →
  ~1.26 s/batch. The loss bound scales with `VITE_TELEMETRY_SAMPLE_RATE` and
  `VITE_TELEMETRY_BATCH_SIZE`.
- **Assumption A2.** A run key of `<startedAt>-<runSeed>` (or a random id) is
  unique in practice; `startRun` already knows both values.
- **Assumption A3.** "Exactly once" is scoped per run; a crashed run's partial is
  never merged into another run.
- **Assumption A4.** Losing the current ring-buffer tail (<1 batch) in addition
  to the in-flight batch is acceptable; a strict one-batch bound would need a
  shorter flush cadence or `bufferCapacity == batchSize`, which can be tuned at
  implementation time if the producer prefers.
- **Priority rationale:** kept `low` — dev-only telemetry that is conveniently
  re-recordable, not product data loss, and not blocking other work. The
  in-memory-sink work already removed the user-facing regression (settings
  becoming unsaveable); this item bounds the residual loss for interrupted dev
  runs.

## Appendix: clarifying questions & answers

- **Q — Which proposed design should be adopted: per-batch part protocol, or a
  heartbeat/checkpoint?** — Answer (agent, repo evidence + item text):
  **part protocol on the existing endpoint** (option 1). It streams every flushed
  batch, so the ≤1-batch bound holds without a separate recovery-on-demand path;
  a heartbeat still needs a reload recovery mechanism and cannot beat the bound
  unless it also fires per batch. Evidence: `src/telemetry/sinks.ts`
  (per-run buffer), `src/telemetry/devUpload.ts` (run-end POST),
  `vite/plugins/telemetryUploadPlugin.ts` (one file + one evaluation per upload).
  **OPEN QUESTION (non-blocking, for the producer at review).**
- **Q — Must the page buffer be preserved for the dev CLI tooling?** — Answer
  (agent, code evidence): yes. `scripts/record-session.mjs`,
  `scripts/capture-gameplay.mjs` and `scripts/verify-dev-telemetry.mjs` read the
  full run through `window.__aiHellTelemetry` **after** the run ends, and
  `verify-dev-telemetry.mjs` asserts the buffer is non-empty
  (`happySinkChars > 0`). The design therefore streams deltas via a watermark and
  never clears the sink mid-run. Evidence: `scripts/verify-dev-telemetry.mjs`
  L~147, `src/scenes/PlayScene.ts` `_initTelemetry`/`flushAndUploadDevTelemetry`.
- **Q — Is a full duplicate of an existing item?** — Answer (worklog search:
  `telemetry upload crash resilience batch`, `incremental batch upload dev
  server`, completed-item scan): no full duplicate. The in-memory-sink item
  (AH-0MVIRYGD1000JVY3, completed) explicitly deferred this; the CLI salvage item
  (AH-0MVVH57LL00038WQ, plan_complete) is a partial overlap scoped to the CLI's
  mid-run-close UX; AH-0MVN06MS9007LRKE / AH-0MVNVGP55002G0KH are the bounded-
  upload predecessors. Duplicate check performed — no overlapping completed item.
- **Q — Where should parts live server-side, and must a crashed run be
  evaluated?** — Answer (agent, code evidence): stage parts under
  `recordings/parts/<runKey>.jsonl` (outside the `session-*.jsonl` glob that
  `verify-dev-telemetry.mjs`/`recordings()` match), rename to the existing
  collision-safe `recordings/session-<stamp>.jsonl` on finalise, and enqueue one
  evaluation only on finalise. A crashed run's partial stays valid NDJSON for
  manual inspection/evaluation but is not auto-evaluated. Evidence:
  `vite/plugins/telemetryUploadPlugin.ts` `storeRecording`, `handleUpload`;
  `scripts/verify-dev-telemetry.mjs` `recordings()`.
  **OPEN QUESTION (non-blocking, for the producer at review).**
- **Q — What is the precise loss bound?** — Answer (agent, analysis): at defaults
  a hard crash loses the in-flight batch (≤64 records / ~1.3 s) **plus** the ring
  buffer's unflushed tail (<64 records), worst case ≈127 records / ~2.5 s,
  typically ≤64 records / ~1.3 s; everything confirmed by the server survives.
  The bound holds while the server is reachable; during an outage the backlog
  stays in memory and is retried at run end. **OPEN QUESTION (non-blocking,
  slightly wider than the item's "~64 records" phrasing).**
- **Q — Does this conflict with the CLI salvage item's boundary?** — Answer
  (agent, worklog): no hard conflict. AH-0MVVH57LL00038WQ's decision D1 already
  states that if page streaming ships first its checkpoint becomes redundant and
  its salvage message should point at the server-side partial. This item's AC3
  keeps `record-session` behaviour unchanged, so both can land in either order;
  ordering should be noted when either is implemented.

# Implement the Music System defined by the Audio Design Chapter

## Goal

Build the runtime background-music system for AI Hell against the fixed design contract captured in
`docs/AUDIO_DESIGN_CHAPTER.md` (produced by **Update GDD with Audio Design Chapter (AH-0MVAUUV1U005UM4W)**).

User story: *As a player, I want a dynamic, retro-arcade soundtrack that responds to combat intensity, so
that runs feel like the relentless survival experience the game is aiming for; and as a developer I want the
music engine driven by a documented parameter/state contract, so behaviour is testable and reproducible.*

> **Scope stance:** this is **future scope, out of MVP** (GDD §8). The MVP ships baked ToneForge SFX only
> (GDD §7.3), and §7.3 remains authoritative for SFX. This item must **not** be started until the design
> chapter exists and has been reviewed, and it must **not** promote music into the MVP without an explicit
> producer decision.

## Background

- AI Hell currently has **no background music** by design: GDD §7.3 keeps music out of MVP scope, and the
  player-fire grid is deliberately quantised to a **silent internal 80 BPM beat** (AH-0MUAYB8EH005RJ8B).
- SFX are build-time baked WAV assets rendered deterministically by ToneForge and played through Phaser's
  shared `AudioContext` (`src/audio/effects.ts`); the authoritative cue catalogue is
  `docs/AUDIO_TONEFORGE_CUE_MAPPING.md`.
- The Audio Design Chapter specifies the musical identity (Phrygian Dominant combat scale, Lydian ambient
  scale, Combat Motifs A/B, "Star Drift"), instrumentation palette, dynamic-mixing rules, state-driven
  transitions, parameter mapping, audio budget and accessibility requirements.

## Expected behaviour and outcomes

- A music system that plays layered/stemmed music driven by an explicit game-state parameter, with
  bar-boundary transitions, stingers, and ducking, as specified by the chapter.
- Music state follows gameplay (e.g. menu/attract, wave combat, boss, low-health tension, run end) with the
  transition rules and timings given in the chapter, and never disrupts the beat grid or the SFX mix.
- Reproducible, deterministic behaviour suitable for automated tests; no audio regressions to the shipped SFX
  pipeline.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] **AC1 — Contract traceable to the chapter:** every implemented music state, transition, stinger and mixing parameter traces to a named section of `docs/AUDIO_DESIGN_CHAPTER.md`, recorded in a mapping table in the implementation docs.
- [ ] **AC2 — Musical content matches the documented identity:** the delivered cues/stems use the chapter's scales, motifs and progressions (Phrygian Dominant combat, Lydian ambient, Combat Motifs A/B, "Star Drift"), verified by an explicit audit table (motif → scale degrees → usage state).
- [ ] **AC3 — State machine implemented and tested:** transitions occur only at the documented boundaries (bar boundaries unless a stinger cut-in is specified), with unit tests covering each transition in the chapter's transition matrix, including invalid/reset paths.
- [ ] **AC4 — Dynamic mixing implemented:** ducking, per-layer volume targets and the priority tiers behave as specified; SFX intelligibility is preserved (music ducks under key SFX cues) and is covered by tests.
- [ ] **AC5 — Autoplay and accessibility compliance:** no audio before a user gesture (`AudioContext` resume discipline, GDD §7.3); the chapter's accessibility requirements (e.g. music/SFX independent volume, mute, and any reduction options) are implemented and documented.
- [ ] **AC6 — Budget met:** the shipped music respects the chapter's audio budget (memory, streaming, polyphony, layer count) on the supported targets, measured and recorded.
- [ ] **AC7 — Docs updated:** GDD §7.3 and §8 are updated to reflect the shipped music system, and `docs/AUDIO_DESIGN_CHAPTER.md` is marked as implemented for the sections that ship.
- [ ] **AC8 — No SFX regression:** the existing ToneForge baked-SFX pipeline and cue catalogue remain unchanged and their tests pass; any chapter §6.4 procedural SFX recipes are explicitly **not** adopted unless decisioned separately.
- [ ] **AC9 — Full project build and test suite pass.**

## Constraints

- **Blocked by** the docs item **Update GDD with Audio Design Chapter (AH-0MVAUUV1U005UM4W)** — this item
  must not begin before `docs/AUDIO_DESIGN_CHAPTER.md` exists.
- Music stays **out of MVP scope** until a producer decision promotes it (GDD §7.3, §8).

Candidate D's *States* section (`docs/OUTER_LOOP_CANDIDATES.md` § Candidate D → States) defines a ring win as **all six hexes held and the AI's massed counter-attack on the hangar repelled**, and a campaign loss as **the hangar falls** (the last hex taken and the hangar's own defence failing). The MVP build (AH-0MVU3VNJI00066YE) deliberately ships the narrower rule, decided by the producer on 2026-10-30 (intake question Q2 = a):

- **Ring secured = every hex of the current ring held.** The next ring then opens.
- **No massed hangar assault** is resolved or played.
- **No hangar-falls lose state**: the hangar itself can never be lost in the MVP, so a player cannot lose the campaign.

## Goal (user story)

As a player, I want the ring to end with a real fight for the hangar — a massed AI counter-attack I have to repel, and a defeat condition that means the hangar can actually fall — so that holding the whole ring feels like a victory rather than the start of the next checklist.

## Desired change

- When the last hex of a ring is captured, **resolve an algorithmic hangar assault** from stored numbers (defender ratings of the held ring vs. the AI's massed force scaled by frontier aggression) — no live simulated battle, matching Candidate D's algorithmic-resolution rule.
- A repelled assault = the ring win state (existing) **plus** a legible report of the numbers.
- A failed assault = **the hangar falls**: define the consequence (restart the current ring with the hangar's unlocks kept, or a documented alternative) and make the reset legible in the defence report.
- Record the chosen win/lose semantics in GDD §8 and `docs/OUTER_LOOP_CANDIDATES.md`.
- Pure resolver logic, exercised in the existing `GymHexWar` gym; gym↔game parity per AGENTS.md; attract mode must not stall (no live battle).

## Acceptance criteria

1. Capturing the ring's final hex triggers an algorithmic hangar-assault resolution from stored numbers, with a report showing the numbers that produced the result.
2. A repelled assault marks the ring won; a failed assault applies the documented hangar-falls consequence.
3. The resolver is a pure module exercised in the gym, with unit tests for repel, fall and boundary cases, and `docs/GYM_PARITY.md` updated if the gym surface changes.
4. The attract bot traverses or skips the assault report without stalling.
5. GDD §8 and `docs/OUTER_LOOP_CANDIDATES.md` record the win/lose semantics; build and full suite green; all related documentation updated.
6. Full project test suite must pass with the new changes.

## Context

Deferred by producer decision during intake of AH-0MVU3VNJI00066YE (2026-10-30, question Q2 = a). Design of record: `docs/OUTER_LOOP_CANDIDATES.md` Candidate D (States, Minimal first slice) and GDD §8.

# Interruption seam and hermetic crash-path tests

**Parent:** AH-0MVVH57LL00038WQ — Recorder silently loses a session when the browser is closed instead of Ctrl+C.
**Slice:** test-first — this child lands the testable seam plus the interruption/lost-message behaviour that child 2 (checkpointed partial capture) and child 3 (usage/docs) build on.

## Goal

As a **maintainer of the recording tooling**, I want the interruption path to be a testable seam (injected page/fs/clock), so the crash path cannot regress into a raw Playwright stack again.

Today `main()` in `scripts/record-session.mjs` inlines the poll loop and the single post-loop buffer read/write, and only SIGINT/SIGTERM are treated as stops. A `page.waitForTimeout` / `page.evaluate` rejection from a closed page escapes to the top-level handler, prints the raw Playwright message and exits 1 with nothing written and no path named. `scripts/record-session.test.ts` cannot reach any of that without a real browser.

## Scope

- Extract from `main()` and export, fully injectable (page `evaluate`, fs writes, clock):
  - `runRecordingWaitLoop({ evaluate, stop, now, wait, maxDurationMs, pollMs, auto })` → a **stop reason** (`'sigint'`, `'run_end'`, `'max_duration'`, `'target_closed'`), classifying a thrown target-closed failure as `'target_closed'` and consulting `page.isClosed()` / `browser.isConnected()` where available (match the known target-closed message family; any unknown failure defaults to the interruption path, never a raw stack).
  - The interruption finaliser: on `'target_closed'` with nothing captured, print exactly one actionable line naming the resolved output path that was not written plus the Ctrl+C procedure, and return exit code 1. On a clean stop, write the final recording and remove any partial (partial *creation* is child 2; this child makes the removal/salvage decision point exist and be tested).
- New `scripts/record-session.test.ts` (`@vitest-environment node`, temp dirs via `mkdtempSync`, **no real browser**): injected `evaluate`/fs/clock fakes.
- Declare every new export in `scripts/record-session.d.mts`.
- Reuse, do not reimplement: `readDevTelemetryChunk` / `readDevTelemetryBufferInChunks` from `scripts/capture-gameplay.mjs`; mirror the salvage/partial idiom of `scripts/capture-salvage.mjs` and the `<stem>.partial.*` naming of `scripts/capture-chunk-sink.mjs`.

## Acceptance Criteria

1. **The interruption path is covered by hermetic tests.** New tests (`scripts/record-session.test.ts`, node environment, no real browser — page/fs/clock injected) prove: (a) a target-closed error thrown from the poll loop routes to the salvage path and not to a raw error exit; (b) with zero captured bytes the lost message names the output path and the Ctrl+C procedure; (c) a clean stop writes the final file and removes the partial. `scripts/recording-cli.test.ts` keeps passing.
2. The wait/finalise logic of `scripts/record-session.mjs` is exported as injectable functions (page `evaluate`, fs writes and clock injected) so the crash, salvage and clean-stop paths are covered hermetically in `scripts/record-session.test.ts` — no real browser in the suite.
3. A target-closed error thrown from the poll loop routes to the interruption/rescue path and never surfaces a raw Playwright target-closed message as the only diagnostic; the process exits non-zero.
4. With zero captured bytes the recorder prints exactly one actionable line — `Recording lost: the browser was closed before Ctrl+C — run npm run record and press Ctrl+C to save` — naming the resolved output path that was not written; proven in `scripts/record-session.test.ts`.
5. On a clean stop the final recording is written and no partial file remains, proven in `scripts/record-session.test.ts`.
6. `scripts/record-session.d.mts` declares every newly exported helper and the type check passes.
7. No behavioural change to `--auto`, `--seed`, `--bot`, `--bot-config`, `--json`, `--poll`, `--max-duration` or `balance-stats.json` on the clean path; the printed success lines are unchanged.

**Key Files:**
- `scripts/record-session.mjs` — wait loop, stop reasons, target-closed classification, interruption finaliser, `--help` block.
- `scripts/record-session.test.ts` *(new)* — the hermetic seam tests.
- `scripts/record-session.d.mts` — declarations for the new exports.
- `scripts/capture-gameplay.mjs` — `readDevTelemetryChunk` / `readDevTelemetryBufferInChunks` (reused, not modified).
- `scripts/capture-salvage.mjs`, `scripts/capture-chunk-sink.mjs` — pattern reference only.

## Notes

- Tests write only into `mkdtempSync` temp dirs (suite-write guard AH-0MVS9TY0N0034LZT); the suite never dirties the checkout.
- No new runtime dependency; node built-ins plus the already-imported Playwright/Vite modules only.
- Checkpoint-append tests (parent AC2(d)/(e)) land in child 2 with the checkpoint implementation; this child's test (a) asserts the routing, not the partial bytes. "Salvage path" in these ACs means this single rescue/finalise seam — the partial-writing branch it calls lands in child 2.

# Checkpointed crash-safe partial capture and salvage

**Parent:** AH-0MVVH57LL00038WQ — Recorder silently loses a session when the browser is closed instead of Ctrl+C.
**Depends on:** child 1 (interruption seam and hermetic crash-path tests).

## Goal

As a **developer recording a long human session**, when I close the browser window (or the page crashes) instead of pressing Ctrl+C, I want whatever was captured saved to a documented partial file, so an hour of play is not lost outright.

The run lives only in the page's in-memory buffer (`window.__aiHellTelemetry`); today `main()` drains it to disk once, after the wait loop, so a closed page has nothing to read. Checkpoint the buffer incrementally to `<output>.partial.jsonl` while recording and finalise that partial as the salvaged session when the page dies.

## Scope

- Resolve the recording output path (`resolveRecordingOutputPath`) **before** the browser launches, so the partial path exists at crash time; the default `session-<timestamp>.jsonl` stamp becomes the **start** time.
- Add `--checkpoint-ms MS` (default `15000`, `0` disables) to `parseRecordArgs`, the flag table and the `--help` block.
- Checkpoint writer: on each interval, read **only new bytes** via the incremental `readDevTelemetryChunk` offset loop (reuse the seam; never a whole-buffer single CDP message — AH-0MVNVGP55002G0KH), append only up to the last newline (never a half-written record; carry the remainder into the next read), and restart from offset 0 when the reported `total` shrinks (the game started a new run — never mix two runs in one file, mirroring `readDevTelemetryBufferInChunks`).
- On a `target_closed` stop, finalise the partial as the salvaged session: collision-safe name (numeric suffix) so a salvage never overwrites an existing final recording (mirror the dev-upload plugin's collision-safe storage), print **one** actionable line naming the partial path and the Ctrl+C stop procedure, exit 1. Do **not** write `balance-stats.json` for a salvaged partial.
- On a clean stop (Ctrl+C / run end / `--max-duration`): write the final file exactly as today, remove the partial, write `balance-stats.json` as today, exit 0.

## Acceptance Criteria

1. **Browser close mid-recording never silently discards the session.** When the page/browser closes (or crashes) during the wait loop, the recorder writes whatever telemetry had been captured — at least the last checkpointed records, each a complete newline-terminated record that parses through the existing recording reader (`parseTelemetryJsonl` / `parseRecording`), never a half-written line — to the documented partial path (`<output>.partial.jsonl`, collision-safe) and prints **one** actionable line naming that path and the Ctrl+C stop procedure; the process exits non-zero. The checkpoint appends only new bytes and restarts at offset 0 when the reported buffer `total` shrinks (no two-run mixing), and a salvage never overwrites an existing final recording — both proven in `scripts/record-session.test.ts`. On a clean stop (Ctrl+C / run end / `--max-duration`) the final recording is byte-identical to today's output, no partial file remains, the exit code is unchanged, and no `balance-stats.json` is written for a salvaged partial.
2. `scripts/record-session.test.ts` proves the checkpoint appends only new bytes and restarts at offset 0 when the reported buffer `total` shrinks (no two-run mixing).
3. `scripts/record-session.test.ts` proves a salvage never overwrites an existing final recording (collision-safe numeric suffix).
4. `--checkpoint-ms` (default 15000, `0` disables) is parsed, covered by `scripts/recording-cli.test.ts` argument-parsing assertions, and passed through to the checkpoint writer.
5. The checkpoint appends only new bytes through the incremental `readDevTelemetryChunk` offset loop — no per-tick full re-read of the buffer, no unbounded in-process buffering — and every written line parses through `parseTelemetryJsonl`.
6. A salvaged partial and its message are additive: the clean-path success output, `balance-stats.json` and exit code are exactly as today.

**Key Files:**
- `scripts/record-session.mjs` — output path resolved up front, `--checkpoint-ms`, checkpoint writer, salvage finaliser, stop-reason handling.
- `scripts/record-session.test.ts` — checkpoint append/reset and no-overwrite tests.
- `scripts/record-session.d.mts` — declarations for new exports and the `checkpointMs` option.
- `scripts/capture-gameplay.mjs` — `readDevTelemetryChunk` / `readDevTelemetryBufferInChunks` (reused, not modified).
- `docs/dev/recording-and-replay.md` — flag row added to the table (prose/behaviour documented in child 3).

## Notes

- Recordings and partials stay under the gitignored `recordings/`; tests write only into `mkdtempSync` temp dirs.
- Long-run cost risk: one CDP round-trip plus a small append per interval; the final read still uses the existing whole-buffer chunked reader. Measurement is child 4.
- This child extends child 1's single rescue seam with the partial-writing branch; it does not add a second failure path.
- If AH-0MVJUAADW0033QBD (page → dev-server streaming) ships first, this local checkpoint becomes redundant and the salvage message should point at the server-side partial — a follow-up, not part of this child.
data.title: Checkpointed crash-safe partial capture and salvage

# Recorder stop procedure in usage text and docs

**Parent:** AH-0MVVH57LL00038WQ — Recorder silently loses a session when the browser is closed instead of Ctrl+C.
**Depends on:** child 2 (checkpointed crash-safe partial capture and salvage) — the docs must describe the behaviour that actually ships.

## Goal

As a **developer reading the tooling**, I want `npm run record --help` and the recording docs to state the stop procedure (Ctrl+C saves; closing the window does not save a completed recording) and the correct `--auto` invocation, so the mistake is avoidable in the first place.

## Scope

- `scripts/record-session.mjs` `--help` text: press Ctrl+C in the terminal to finish and save; closing the browser window ends the recording and at best salvages a partial file; `--auto` must be passed after `--` (`npm run record -- --auto`); list `--checkpoint-ms`.
- `scripts/recording-cli.test.ts`: extend the existing `--help`/usage assertions to pin the new lines (spawned-CLI assertion as today).
- `docs/dev/recording-and-replay.md` §1: flag table row for `--checkpoint-ms`, and rewrite the Ctrl+C paragraph — the existing claim that "on Ctrl+C the tool still exports whatever the sink has already flushed … so an interrupted run yields a partial but valid recording" must state the partial-path and partial-vs-final semantics, the salvage/lost behaviour and the stop procedure.
- `docs/TELEMETRY.md`: the recorder paragraphs (buffer-read description) must name the partial path, the checkpoint flag, the salvage/lost behaviour and the stop procedure.
- Any README or code-comment text that describes the recorder's stop behaviour is updated to match.

## Acceptance Criteria

1. **Usage text and docs state the stop requirement.** `npm run record --help` (and `node scripts/record-session.mjs --help`) states the Ctrl+C-to-save requirement, that closing the browser window does not save a completed recording (at best a partial), and the `npm run record -- --auto` separator form; asserted by a test on the help output.
2. **Documentation.** `docs/dev/recording-and-replay.md` §1 (flag table + the Ctrl+C paragraph) documents the partial path, partial-vs-final semantics, the salvage/lost behaviour, the `--checkpoint-ms` flag and the stop procedure.
3. The recorder paragraphs in `docs/TELEMETRY.md` document the same partial path, `--checkpoint-ms` flag, salvage/lost behaviour and stop procedure.
4. All related documentation is updated to reflect the changes, including code comments, README, and any relevant wiki or docs site entries; no doc still claims an interrupted run always yields a valid complete recording.
5. `scripts/recording-cli.test.ts` asserts the new usage lines and keeps the existing argument-parsing assertions passing.

**Key Files:**
- `scripts/record-session.mjs` — `--help` block.
- `scripts/recording-cli.test.ts` — usage/help assertions.
- `docs/dev/recording-and-replay.md` §1 — flag table and Ctrl+C paragraph.
- `docs/TELEMETRY.md` — recorder buffer-read / dev-tooling paragraphs.
- `./README.md` — only if it describes the recorder's stop behaviour.

## Notes

- Docs describe shipped behaviour only — this child lands after child 2, and must not document speculative flags.
- No repository-boundary edits (`.pi/`, `skill/`, `command/`).

# Real-browser salvage verification and checkpoint cost check

**Parent:** AH-0MVVH57LL00038WQ — Recorder silently loses a session when the browser is closed instead of Ctrl+C.
**Depends on:** child 2 (checkpointed crash-safe partial capture and salvage), child 3 (usage text and docs).

## Goal

As a **maintainer**, I want end-to-end evidence that a real browser close mid-recording salvages a usable partial (not just a mocked one), that the checkpoint interval's CDP + append cost is acceptable on a long run, and that the clean path is still byte-identical — so the stringly target-closed detection and the checkpoint interval default are validated against reality rather than assumed.

## Scope

- Drive a real (headless is fine) recording through `scripts/record-session.mjs` (or the shipped `npm run record`), close the browser mid-recording, and confirm: one actionable first line naming the partial path, exit code 1, and a partial file whose every line parses through `parseTelemetryJsonl` / `parseRecording`.
- Confirm the lost-message branch end-to-end (browser closed before any checkpoint, e.g. `--checkpoint-ms` larger than the run duration or with no telemetry read possible).
- Measure the checkpoint cost on a long run (30-minute budget or a scaled equivalent with a documented extrapolation): CDP round-trips and bytes appended per interval, peak RSS, and the final whole-buffer read; record whether `--checkpoint-ms 15000` stays the default.
- Verify clean-path parity: a Ctrl+C / `--auto` recording produces byte-identical output to the pre-change recorder (compare against a recording made on the parent commit) and no partial file remains.
- Record all evidence (commands, timings, exit codes, file sizes, sample first line) as comments on this work item.

## Acceptance Criteria

1. **Full project test suite must pass with the new changes.** The dev-push gate's full suite runs green, including `scripts/record-session.test.ts` and `scripts/recording-cli.test.ts`.
2. A real-browser interruption run (browser closed mid-recording) salvages a partial file that parses through `parseTelemetryJsonl` / `parseRecording`, prints one actionable first line naming that path and the Ctrl+C procedure, and exits non-zero — evidence recorded on this work item.
3. A real-browser run closed before any checkpoint captures nothing, prints exactly one actionable line naming the resolved output path that was not written and the Ctrl+C procedure, and exits non-zero — evidence recorded on this work item.
4. On a clean stop (Ctrl+C / run end / `--max-duration`) the final recording is byte-identical to the pre-change recorder's output for the same seed, no partial file remains, `balance-stats.json` is still written and the exit code is unchanged — evidence recorded on this work item.
5. Checkpoint cost for a long run (30-minute budget or a documented scaled equivalent) is measured and recorded — CDP round-trips per interval, bytes appended, peak RSS — with the `--checkpoint-ms` default confirmed or a tuned default proposed on this work item.
6. Any risk or divergence found (target-closed error-shape differences across Playwright surfaces, checkpoint cost, leftover partials) is recorded as a comment, and a `discovered-from:AH-0MVVH57LL00038WQ` work item is created for anything out of scope.

**Key Files:**
- `scripts/record-session.mjs` — the tool under verification (no changes expected unless a measurement shows the default needs tuning).
- `scripts/inspect-telemetry.mjs`, `scripts/recording.mjs` — `parseTelemetryJsonl` / `parseRecording` used to validate the salvaged partial.
- `docs/dev/recording-and-replay.md` — flag default and stop procedure confirmed against the measured behaviour.

## Notes

- Long-running commands here follow the shared background-job etiquette (launch → prepare → one completion-aware wait via `skill/shared/wait_for_job.py` → collect).
- All agent test runs go through the test skill (`/skill:test`); the full-suite gate is the dev-push hook.
- Recordings written during verification stay under the gitignored `recordings/`; nothing tracked is dirtied.

# Context

The ring-timing harness (AH-0MVUXCBQY001ESWT) measured both Hangar War ring
budgets with the headless arena. Both land inside the design windows (ring 1:
**43.7 min** in 40–60; ring 2: **91.6 min** in 70–100), but ring 2's
composition is lopsided.

- Ring 2's authored aggression floor is **3** (`src/data/hex-ring-2.csv`), which
  the shipped `hexAggressionLevel` mapping resolves to campaign level 4 — the
  first level where enemies fire. The competent bot survives the full
  ≈5-minute deployment window at levels 1–3 and loses every run at level 4+, so
  **all 12 ring-2 deployments are first-attempt losses**.
- The ring-2 total is therefore dominated by the modelled retry allowance
  (**60 of 91.6 min**), not by measured deployment time (7.6 min). The design's
  estimate of "≈60 minutes of deployments plus 10–40 minutes of builds and
  losses" does not hold at ring 2's authored aggressions.

Evidence: `docs/dev/ring-timing-baseline.json` (seeds 1–3, competent bot) and
`docs/EVALUATION.md` § Ring timing harness.

# Goal

As a maintainer, I want ring 2's aggression floor reviewed against the design's
deployments-vs-losses split, so ring 2 is *harder* rather than *uniformly
lost* — without changing the 70–100-minute budget.

# Scope (proposal, needs producer review)

- Decide whether every ring-2 hex being a first-attempt loss is intended
  difficulty or an aggression-floor authoring artefact.
- If tuning is wanted: lower some ring-2 base aggressions (e.g. a survivable
  band at level 2–3 for the weaker hexes, keeping the weapon hex the hardest)
  and re-run `npm run ring-timing` to re-baseline.
- Any change must keep the ring-2 budget inside 70–100 min and the weapon hex
  strictly the ring's hardest (the ring-definition validation pins that).

# Acceptance criteria

- A recorded decision (keep as intended, or a tuned ring-2 aggression floor with
  a regenerated `docs/dev/ring-timing-baseline.json`).
- If tuned: ring 1 and ring 2 grind budgets still in-window, the weapon hex is
  still the hardest, and the full suite is green.
- `docs/EVALUATION.md` § Ring timing harness reflects the outcome.
data.title: Review ring 2 aggression floor against the measured builds/losses split

As a player, I want occasional **special missions** whose rewards are special (a new hull type with extra hit points or extra upgrade bays, rather than another currency drop), so that the ring is never a six-chore checklist.

Part of the Hangar War's **post-MVP mitigation backlog** (discovered-from:AH-0MVU3VNJI00066YE, recorded in `docs/OUTER_LOOP_CANDIDATES.md` Candidate D and GDD §8.2). Deliberately **out of scope** for Build Candidate D's MVP (AH-0MVU3VNJI00066YE); captured so the design intent is not lost.

- A special-mission hex/mission type with a reward outside the shipped salvage currencies: a new hull type (extra hit points or extra upgrade bays) is the reference example.
- Must reuse the shipped deployment path (`PlayScene` + `src/scenes/core/`) and the pure hangar economy; no second run implementation (AGENTS.md gym↔game parity).

- A special mission is offered, described (reward known ahead) and completable through the shipped run.


The GDD §8.2 table those assertions guard is a *transcription* of `docs/dev/ring-timing-baseline.json` (the artifact the same test already asserts is cited). So every legitimate arena recalibration requotes the artifact and the GDD together, and strands the guard until someone hand-edits four more numbers — which is exactly what happened twice:

- AH-0MVXSHAS100010S0 (ring-2 budget/measurements) — no, stale only after the wrap-aware bot landed;
- AH-0MVMISF0Q00314LG (wrap-aware bot) raised the measured grind 91.6 → 109.0 min;
- AH-0MW09QIJU000DAGT (commit `a7c57da1`) recalibrated the ring-2 window to 90–120 min and regenerated the artifact, leaving the guard red until commit `032d96e9`.

The failure was caught (good), but the literals are the wrong source of truth: the guard should assert *agreement with the artifact*, not a copy of it.

## Desired change

In `src/outerLoopCandidatesDocs.test.ts`:

1. Read `docs/dev/ring-timing-baseline.json` (the path the guard already requires the GDD to cite) and derive the expected one-decimal mean for each `ringIndex`/`strategy` pair (`1-grind`, `2-grind`, `1-rush`, `2-rush`) from `summary.totalMinutes.mean.toFixed(1)`.
2. Assert the GDD §8.2 prose quotes each of those four values with its unit (`<mean> min`), so the GDD can never drift from the artifact.
3. Keep the window (40–60, 90–120) and tolerance (±2 / ±3 min) assertions explicit — those are design values owned by `RING_TIMING_TARGETS` / `RING_TIMING_TOLERANCE_PERCENT`, not measurements.

A working implementation was written and verified green (full suite 419 files / 9517 tests) during AH-0MW0J01VV0054BRR but dropped because the sibling item landed the literal-pinning form first; the parked commit is `9467a48a` (ref `refs/wip/AH-0MW0J01VV0054BRR`) if the shape is useful.

## Acceptance Criteria

1. The guard's four measured-mean assertions are derived from `docs/dev/ring-timing-baseline.json`; no measured-mean literal remains in the test.
2. Editing a mean in the artifact alone (without the GDD) fails the guard; editing the GDD to a value the artifact does not hold fails the guard.
3. The window and tolerance assertions are unchanged and still pass.
4. Full project test suite passes.
